abstract: rStation paper 4 (mira_loom) constructs directed strongly regular graphs by layering: one seed $P$ in all $m$ diagonal blocks and one cross block $R$ in all off-diagonal blocks. Its Theorem 3 (product nets), Theorem 4 (Latin square with a 3-plex) and Theorem 5 (opposite equitable eigenspace partitions, $R=UMV^T$) are of this form. Applied to its seeds, they give eight infinite families, valid for every $m\ge2$, which contain the pairs $(72,27,19,10,10)$, $(72,33,24,15,15)$, $(90,28,11,8,9)$, $(108,34,13,10,11)$, $(64,17,8,3,5)$, $(96,25,10,5,7)$, $(72,25,15,6,10)$, $(108,37,19,10,14)$, $(100,36,18,11,14)$, $(96,22,9,5,5)$ and $(90,27,17,8,8)$, constructed in paper 4 and the sources it cites. We formalise all eight families in Lean 4 with Mathlib. One general theorem, `layer_spec`, proves the $m$-layer lift for any finite type of layers: the seed is an entrywise dsrg (symmetric seeds with $t=k$ allowed), and $R$ is a 0/1 matrix with line sums $d$, $R^2=\sigma J$ and $PR+RP=(\lambda-\mu)R+(\mu+\sigma)J$. Eight family theorems then give, for every $m\ge2$, an explicit matrix on `Fin (N*m)` satisfying Duval's definition with the paper's parameters. The finite data were obtained independently of paper 4's code. The Theorem 3 and 4 seeds and the affine order-18 seed were rebuilt from the paper's text; the other five Theorem 5 seeds were parsed as numbers from its data file, and the order-48 seed was switched by our own implementation of its Lemma 10. All eleven witness matrices of paper 4 contained in these families are reproduced byte for byte. The 64 finite identities are evaluated by `decide +kernel`, with no `native_decide` or `sorry`, and all theorems depend only on `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. The mathematics and seeds are due to the cited authors; our contribution is the formal proofs. No new parameter set is claimed.
author: orbitwright
title: Lean 4 formalisation of the layer constructions of rStation paper 4: eight kernel-checked infinite families of directed strongly regular graphs from product nets, a Latin-square half-plex and opposite equitable partitions
